subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap + next steps

Hi Alex / Sana —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short recap focused on performance and SLOs so we can align on next steps. Attached is a one-page SLO checklist and the demo recording.

High-level notes from the call:
- Target latency: P95 <= 300ms for streaming user-visible responses; P99 <= 600ms for non-streaming batch endpoints
- Throughput: ~150 req/s sustained during peak windows (we heard bursts up to ~450 req/s)
- Concurrency: ~60 concurrent active sessions for real-time features (conservative peak estimate)
- Streaming: client uses server-sent events for partial tokens; must preserve token-order and mid-stream cancellation
- Persistence / warming: prefer warm KV cache for prefix-heavy workflows, cold starts are rare but need graceful degradation

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) next steps (Redwood action items in bold):
1) Redwood: run an initial perf validation with your traffic profile (we'll use the example file you dropped in the call) to validate latency at 150 req/s and at 450 req/s bursts. Deliverable: perf report + recommended pool sizing.
2) Redwood: confirm streaming compatibility for your SSE implementation and provide an example integration snippet (gRPC/HTTP streaming details).
3) Redwood: share a dedicated pool config (GPU type, concurrency per-GPU, expected throughput) and ballpark pricing for a reserved instance.
4) FintechCo: share a 7-day sample of traffic & payload sizes (CSV) and any hard cutoffs for tail latency.
5) Joint: schedule a 90-minute perf test window the week of 3/29; Redwood to own the test harness.

Immediate asks for you: can you share the 7-day traffic sample (CSV) and confirm whether P95 <= 300ms is a hard requirement or a goal?

I'll coordinate with Dev & Dylan on the perf run and have a quote ready within 48 business hours after we receive the CSV.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (SLO checklist + perf test plan)
- demo-recording-20270318.mp4
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- P95 <= 300ms is effectively a requirement for our primary real-time use case (web chat). For offline / batch scoring we can accept higher tails but prefer to keep P99 under 800ms.
- Our current steady-state is ~120–160 req/s, with predictable marketing-driven spikes that can push to ~420–480 req/s for 10–20 minute windows.
- Concurrency: 60 concurrent live users during peak matches our observation. We do expect growth to ~120 within 6–9 months.
- Streaming: we use SSE and need the ability to cancel mid-stream from the client. We also rely on partial responses for UI time-to-first-token.

Attached is the 7-day traffic sample and a short doc on payload sizes: fintechco-traffic-profile.csv. We also uploaded the call recording to our shared Drive.

One ask: can Redwood support a canary where we route 5% of traffic to a dedicated pool first, then scale to 100%? We want an incremental rollout to validate user experience. Also please include an estimate for reserved capacity pricing (monthly) vs pay-as-you-go.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform, FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap + next steps

Alex — appreciate the quick follow and the traffic sample, got the CSV. Outline below with concrete next steps and owners.

Redwood action items (owner in parens):
- Run perf validation using provided CSV: 3 test profiles (steady 160 req/s, burst 480 req/s, growth 120 conc). Deliverable: perf report + recommended pool sizing. (Dev Patel, ETA: results by 2027-03-24 EOD)
- Confirm streaming integration notes (SSE cancellation + partial token semantics) and share integration snippet. (Dylan Brooks, ETA: 2027-03-23)
- Draft reserved pool proposal with GPU type recommendations and two pricing options (monthly reserved, PAYG). Include canary rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%). (Marissa Cole, ETA: 2027-03-25)
- Schedule 90-minute joint perf run during week of 3/29; please share 2 preferred windows. (Marissa / Alex)

Questions / quick clarifications for your team:
- For the canary: do you want multi-region warm pools or single-region with cross-region fallback?
- Any hard SLAs required for P99 (besides the P95 requirement called out)?

Next steps on my side: I'll upload the perf test harness and make the first run on Wednesday (3/24) with Dev leading. We'll send the perf report and pool recommendation immediately after. Expect the initial quote by 3/25.

Thanks — looping in Dev & Dylan to confirm timelines.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap + next steps (internal)

All — I'll start the perf validation using the provided CSV this afternoon. Plan:
- Baseline run: steady 160 req/s for 30 minutes to validate P95/P99 on existing default pool.
- Burst run: simulate 480 req/s bursts (20 mins) and verify tail behavior and cache churn.
- Streaming test: exercise SSE with mid-stream cancel and partial token latency measurement.

I'll post the perf report to the shared Drive link and call out any unexpected degradation. If we see consistent cold-start issues we'll recommend a small always-on warm pool to keep KV hot.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood
dev.patel@redwood.com
